documents.title: User stories — Skeleton (S02)
documents.body:
# User stories — Skeleton (S02)

## Personas

- **The runtime client** — a person or agent calling the API under exactly one tenant, authenticated through the realm or through the dev principal.
- **The platform engineer** — runs the one binary as `serve`, `migrate`, `worker` or `admin`, and owns the local compose stack.
- **The delivery worker** — the `worker` subcommand that claims jobs, renews its lease and survives a kill.
- **The SSE consumer** — a UI or agent holding `/api/events` open and resuming with `Last-Event-ID`.
- **The later slice builder** — S03–S12 consume the tenancy, auth, job and SSE contracts instead of re-inventing them.
- **The licensing operator** — owns the `app_licence` rows and the `licence.sync` job.
- **The sign-in user, declared for S12** — signs in through OIDC, signs out, switches tenant and reads `/api/me`.

## Stories

- As a runtime client, I want every request scoped to exactly one tenant through my membership, so that no client-supplied header or path can reach another tenant's rows.
- As a platform engineer, I want one binary with `serve | migrate | worker | admin`, so that the skeleton ships as one artifact with one configuration surface.
- As a platform engineer, I want `migrate` to refuse a role that is superuser or `BYPASSRLS`, so that a mis-provisioned database cannot pass a test while production leaks.
- As a delivery worker, I want a fenced lease token, so that a handler outliving `JOB_LEASE_SECS` runs exactly once and a killed worker's work is reclaimed.
- As an SSE consumer, I want replay from `Last-Event-ID` in `seq` order inside my tenant, so that a dropped connection resumes without duplicates or foreign events.
- As the licensing operator, I want a fail-closed `RequireLicence` that reads `app_licence` only, so that an absent, stale or unknown licence refuses without a synchronous call to the licences service.
- As a later slice builder, I want `TenantId` typed into every store function, so that an unscoped query is a compile error rather than a review comment.
- As a sign-in user, I want the declared `shell/login` surface, so that S12 builds sign-in, sign-out, tenant switch and `/api/me` on a fixed contract.

## Scenarios

- Given the two dev tenants `dev-a` and `dev-b`, when a `conveyor_runtime` request scoped to A reads `event`, then it sees none of B's rows; an insert carrying B's `tenant_id` fails the policy `WITH CHECK`; the superuser sees both; the owner role also sees zero, which proves `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`.
- Given a handler that outlives `JOB_LEASE_SECS`, when the renewal loop runs, then `renew` extends the lease only with the same `lease_token`.
- Given a worker killed with `kill -9` mid-handler, when a worker restarts, then the row is reclaimed on lease expiry, `attempts` increments and the stale token writes nothing.
- Given three events, when a client reconnects with `Last-Event-ID`, then the later two arrive once each in `seq` order and B's events are absent.
- Given two concurrent runs, when the schedule materialiser fires under `pg_advisory_xact_lock`, then exactly one job is created.
- Given the `/api/events` route is licence-gated, when there is no `app_licence` row, then the response is a 403 problem+json.
- Given `CONVEYOR_DEV_AUTH` set and `Bearer dev:alice`, when `/api/me` is called, then the principal is `alice` in `dev-a`, resolved through `membership`.
- Given `CONVEYOR_DEV_AUTH` set with `APP_ENV=production`, when the process starts, then it exits non-zero.

## Verify

- `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test rls -- --nocapture` — the two-tenant gate as the runtime role, with the superuser positive control and the owner control that proves `FORCE`.
- `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test jobs_kill` and `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test jobs_lease_two_workers` — the kill/restart and the two-worker exactly-once proofs.
- `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test events` — the SSE replay and its tenant scope.
- `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test schedule` and `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test prune` — one job per materialised schedule and per-tenant prune inside scoped transactions.
- `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test audit_idempotency` — the append-only grant and the idempotency key.
- `cargo test -p conveyor-auth --test licence` — the fail-closed licence verdict.
- `cargo run -p conveyor-server -- --print-openapi` — `/api/events` and the other paths in the emitted document.
- `docker compose up -d --build` then `curl -sf localhost:8930/health/ready` — the composed app on the same port inside and outside.
- The project gate is the S02 acceptance manifest's 16 checks, discharged by the programme record.

## Links

- Plan: `docs/plans/slices/S02-skeleton.md` §3, §5, §6, §7, §9.
- Issue: #2, the P2 long-job proof.
- Record: the S02 project row; `acceptance/programme/S02.toml`; `docs/evidence/rework/S02.json`.

## Notes

Reconstructed from the slice plan and the live record on 2026-11-28 for standard v4. S02 is the delivery narrative of the skeleton every later slice builds on; the P2 long-job proof is the part the retrospective rework added.

documents.title: Acceptance criteria — Skeleton (S02)
documents.body:
# Acceptance criteria — Skeleton (S02)

## Scenarios

- Two tenants isolated, including RLS: as `conveyor_runtime` scoped to A, `count(*) FROM event` returns zero of B's rows; an insert with B's `tenant_id` fails the policy `WITH CHECK`; the superuser sees both; the owner also sees zero.
- Login works: `Bearer dev:alice` returns 200 on `/api/me`; with `APP_ENV=production` and dev auth set the process exits non-zero.
- The job survives a kill: with `JOB_LEASE_SECS=2` and `kill -9` mid-handler, the restarted worker reclaims the row on lease expiry, `attempts` increments and the stale token writes nothing.
- A legitimate long handler runs exactly once: a handler beyond the lease completes once while a second worker polls the same tenant, and renewal at lease/3 is fenced by the claim token.
- SSE replay: three events; a reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` delivers the later two once each in `seq` order and B's events are absent.
- Scheduling and pruning: two concurrent materialisations create one job; prune loops over `event`, `job` and `idempotency_key` run per tenant inside scoped transactions.
- Audit append-only: `UPDATE audit_event` as the runtime role is permission denied.
- Licence fail-closed: no `app_licence` row gives a 403 problem+json; an unknown status gives 403.
- Migrator safety: `migrate` asserts `rolsuper = false AND rolbypassrls = false` and aborts otherwise; the embedded migration set is exactly `[(1, "platform")]`.
- Compose portability: `db` on 5439, `pgbouncer` on 6439 and `app` on 8930 keep the same port inside and outside; integration tests start their own ephemeral container and a container that cannot start fails, never skips.
- The project gate: the A–D artefacts and the delivery contract exist, the brief and evidence are published, the P2 long-job proof is landed and the project closes through the one gate.

## Verify commands

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace`
- `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test rls -- --nocapture`
- `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test jobs_kill`
- `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test jobs_lease_two_workers`
- `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test events`
- `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test schedule`
- `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test prune`
- `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test audit_idempotency`
- `cargo test -p conveyor-auth --test licence`
- `cargo run -p conveyor-server -- --print-openapi`, with `jq -e` over the emitted document checking the `/api/events` path.
- `cargo run -p conveyor-server -- migrate`
- `psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f scripts/db-roles.sql` against the direct owner URL named in `DATABASE_MIGRATE_URL`.
- `docker compose up -d --build` then `curl -sf localhost:8930/health/ready`.
- The S02 acceptance manifest's 16 gate checks, discharged by the programme record at `acceptance/programme/S02.toml`.

## Results

Met. S02 is `status: closed` and `measured_status: built` in the programme seed. The plan's six gate rows are the skeleton's measured target, and the remaining delivery unit, issue #2, landed the P2 two-worker long-handler proof as `apps/server/tests/jobs_lease_two_workers.rs`; P1 (renewal and fencing) and P3 (kill and restart) were already on the merged train. The S02 rework ledger `docs/evidence/rework/S02.json` records 17 checks and 0 failures at `2026-11-26`, including the project close, the approved baseline, the charter gate, the published closure output, the board-approved contract, the compliant Phase-G review, zero active waivers, the PI cadence, plan and objectives, the WSJF inputs, the demo credit and the tranche-1 lesson. Issue #2 is closed.

## Status

met — the plan gate is green and the project closed on the P2 proof at the named SHA.

## Links

- Plan §7 gate table; #2; `acceptance/programme/S02.toml`; `docs/evidence/rework/S02.json`; the S02 project row.

documents.title: Definition of ready — Skeleton (S02)
documents.body:
# Definition of ready — Skeleton (S02)

## Independent

S02 starts from a docs-only repository — no `Cargo.toml`, no `crates/`, no `.git` (CONTRACT §13). Its tree is file-disjoint from S00's `parity.yaml`, which S02 reads and ignores, and from S01's UI ADR, which reserves `apps/web` as empty. The workspace, migration, roles and crates are new files; the only shared inputs are the plan and the contract. The project's delivery unit is the single issue #2.

## Negotiable

The outcome is fixed: a ten-member workspace over Postgres 18 with eleven platform tables under forced RLS, typed tenancy, OIDC and dev auth, a fail-closed licence gate, a fenced job runner and a replaying SSE stream, gated by the requirement that two tenants are isolated including RLS and that login works (SPEC §8 S2). How it is realised was settled in the slice's seven decisions, S2-D1 to S2-D7: `TenantId` in `crates/domain`, superuser-created roles with a migrating assertion, per-tenant prune loops, `pg_notify` as a doorbell, root `migrations/` embedded via `../../migrations`, dev principals resolved through `membership`, and a dependency-free `apps/web` placeholder.

## Valuable

Before S02 the repository is docs-only: no compiling workspace, no database, no authentication boundary. S02 gives every later slice a running substrate — S03's aggregates, S04's action registry, S07's catalogue and `vector`/`pg_trgm` extensions, S12's UI and S14's cluster deploy all sit on these tables, this pool and this binary. It closes the highest-bug-surface risk the contract names (R8, auth and tenancy) and keeps the Redis ban (R6): rate limits and caches are in-process or advisory locks.

## Estimable

Baseline `main` at the S02 claim, docs-only. The plan names every file, the eleven table bodies, the endpoints, the environment variables and the pinned workspace versions, and its build order is eighteen numbered steps with the command for each. §7's six gate rows are the measured target, so effort is sized against proofs rather than prose.

## Small

One workspace, eight crates and two apps, of which `actions`, `actions-derive`, `render` and `workflow` are empty stubs and `apps/web` is a zero-dependency placeholder. Out of scope by the plan: domain aggregates and tables, the action registry, the board, run and approval endpoints, the Keycloak realm beyond `CONVEYOR_OIDC_ISSUER`, the licences service, cluster deploy and pgbouncer config, pgvector and search, the UI, and `.github/`.

## Testable

Every gate row carries an executable proof: the RLS test runs as `conveyor_runtime` with a superuser positive control and an owner control that proves `FORCE`; login is a 200 on `/api/me` plus a non-zero production refusal; the job proof is `JOB_LEASE_SECS=2` with `kill -9` and the two-worker long-handler test; SSE is a `Last-Event-ID` reconnect; the audit is a failing `UPDATE`; the licence is a 403. The workspace gate is `fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, the OpenAPI print, `migrate` and a composed `/health/ready`.

## Dependencies

- blocked-by: S00, the usage inventory and `parity.yaml`, which S02 reads but does not use; and S01, the UI ADR, which reserves `apps/web` as empty.
- blocks: S03 (domain aggregates and tables), S04 (the action registry), S05 and S06 (board, run and approval endpoints), S07 (the catalogue seed and the `vector` and `pg_trgm` extensions), S12 (the UI, including the declared `shell/login` surface), S14 (the Keycloak realm, cluster deploy, pgbouncer config and DBA-created roles).
- related: D12, the licences service, reached only through `LICENCES_BASE_URL` by `licence.sync` and never synchronously on a core request; CONTRACT §9, tenant comes from membership and never a client header; CONTRACT §13, no `.git`, `.github` or `new-rust-target.sh` in this slice.
- environment: a superuser for `scripts/db-roles.sql`, and the pinned `pgvector/pgvector:0.8.7-pg18` image for compose and tests.

## Notes

Reconstructed for standard v4 on 2026-11-28 from the slice plan, the S02 acceptance manifest and the project row.

documents.title: Definition of done — Skeleton (S02)
documents.body:
# Definition of done — Skeleton (S02)

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Verify |
|---|---|
| Two tenants isolated, including RLS | `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test rls -- --nocapture` with the runtime, superuser and owner controls |
| Login works | `Bearer dev:alice` gives 200 on `/api/me`; dev auth with `APP_ENV=production` exits non-zero |
| The job survives a kill | `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test jobs_kill` |
| A handler beyond the lease runs exactly once under two workers | `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test jobs_lease_two_workers` |
| SSE replay in `seq` order with no foreign events | `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test events` |
| One job per schedule; prune stays per tenant | `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test schedule`; `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test prune` |
| Audit is append-only and idempotency keys hold | `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test audit_idempotency` |
| The licence fails closed | `cargo test -p conveyor-auth --test licence` |
| The workspace gate | `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --workspace`; the `--print-openapi` document carried `/api/events`; `cargo run -p conveyor-server -- migrate`; `docker compose up -d --build` with `/health/ready` green |
| The project gate | the 16 checks in `acceptance/programme/S02.toml`, discharged by the record |

## Evidence at completion

S02 is `status: closed` and `measured_status: built`. The programme ledger `docs/evidence/rework/S02.json` records 17 checks and 0 failures at `2026-11-26`, covering the close on the P2 proof, the approved baseline, the charter gate, the published closure output, the board-approved contract, the compliant Phase-G review, zero active waivers, the PI cadence, plan and objectives, the WSJF inputs, the demo credit and the tranche-1 lesson. Issue #2 is closed, and the P2 proof, `apps/server/tests/jobs_lease_two_workers.rs`, is on main.

## Repo gate

The slice gate: `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --workspace`; the `--print-openapi` document carrying `/api/events`; `cargo run -p conveyor-server -- migrate`; `docker compose up -d --build` with `/health/ready` green. The compile and lint verdict at review is the repository's GitHub-hosted preflight and the pull request's CI; a local compiling `cargo` command is not the gate.

## Merge and closure

Issue #2 closed by its one pull request, and S02 closed through the one gate on the P2 proof at the named SHA. The lane branches are deleted after merge. The closure output is published, and the Phase-G review cites the standing delegation. The tranche-1 review remains the sponsoring group's separate act.
